description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis represents ACC (%) on a linear scale from 60 to 80. The 'Base' method is shown as a solid black line with circle markers, starting at approximately 64% ACC at a co-occurrence number of 1 and rising to about 71% at 1000. The 'MEND' method is depicted as a brown dashed line with diamond markers, beginning at about 71% ACC at 1 and increasing to roughly 80% at 1000. The 'FT' method is a blue dashed line with triangle markers, starting at approximately 65% ACC at 1 and ending at about 73% ACC at 1000. The 'MEMIT' method, shown as a purple dashed line with circle markers, begins at roughly 70% ACC at 1 and rises to about 77% ACC at 1000. The 'IKE' method is represented by a red dashed line with triangle markers, starting at approximately 67% ACC at 1 and increasing to about 75% ACC at 1000. The 'ROME' method is a green dashed line with square markers, beginning at approximately 74% ACC at 1 and rising to about 82% ACC at 1000. All lines show a general upward trend with increasing co-occurrence number, with ROME consistently achieving the highest ACC and Base the lowest.
